annotation_type: second AI-agent manual annotation from request text and source schema; not human annotation
prediction_blinding: No historical prediction JSON or new result file was opened while producing this rubric. The inherited task context contains selected previously reported findings (including the music-to-email example); therefore do not describe the annotator as fully blind to all historical outcomes.

scoring.binary: Preserve original four-class fixture and original 100 act / 125 nonact boundary. ASK, OUT_OF_SCOPE and UNKNOWN are nonact; all other validated intent labels are act. Report malformed/error/fallback separately, never silently discard them.
scoring.coarse_actionable_semantics: Use exact membership of the (intent, tool) pair in allowed_pairs for the fixed scorable actionable subset. Do not use independent intent and tool membership, which allows invalid cross-products. Label this coarse route-pair correctness; legacy FILE_ACTION buckets intentionally pool unrelated capabilities.
scoring.native_semantics: Report the fixed native_semantic_scorable subset separately, matching native_semantic_pairs. This avoids treating legacy catch-all FILE_ACTION as a semantically precise intent.
scoring.exact_capability: Unavailable from the router schema: it emits no capability ID and no validated arguments. Denominator is 0, do not report 0% accuracy or substitute coarse route correctness.
scoring.nonaction: All 125 original nonaction rows remain in binary scoring. preferred_intent and tool=none can support separate clarification/OOS analyses; never count UNKNOWN as an explicit refusal.
scoring.errors: A schema-invalid record, missing record or provider fallback must remain visible; report a failure-inclusive fixed-denominator metric and a valid-output diagnostic separately. Do not reward provider failure UNKNOWN as a deliberate refusal. Model exact format compliance is distinct.
